# PlusAI Announces Key Performance Indicators for Commercial Readiness

* PlusAI is demonstrating steady progress toward commercial launch of factory-built autonomous trucks in 2027
* The KPIs reflect SuperDrive’s safety, autonomy, and scalability, backed by real-world testing, proprietary data, and end-to-end AI architecture
* Initial launch is expected to be in the Texas Triangle, then expand to other freight corridors in the U.S. and Europe

Santa Clara, Calif. – July 31, 2025 – PlusAI, an artificial intelligence company commercializing AI-based virtual driver software for factory-built autonomous commercial trucks, today announced the release of its set of key performance indicators (KPIs) designed to track progress towards commercial readiness of SuperDrive™. In the first half of 2025, PlusAI achieved significant advancements in autonomous performance metrics, reaching 86% Safety Case Readiness (SCR), 98% Autonomous Miles Percentage (AMP), and 76% Remote Assistance Free Trips (RAFT), up from 75%, 97%, and 69%, respectively, in the second half of 2024. As PlusAI transitions to a public company, it intends to report these KPIs regularly to provide transparency on its path to commercial launch in Texas in 2027.

For commercial launch, PlusAI is targeting 100% Safety Case Readiness, and more than 90% Remote Assistance-Free Trips. Achieving these milestones will demonstrate that PlusAI’s fully autonomous virtual driver system, SuperDrive, has the safety, performance, and operational efficiency required for real-world commercial deployment, enabling trucking fleet operators to complete entire routes without human intervention. PlusAI is currently conducting public road testing in Texas and Sweden, with customer fleet trials scheduled for the fall of 2025.

“We have a clear roadmap to the commercial launch of SuperDrive,” said David Liu, CEO and Co-Founder of PlusAI. “By publicly sharing these performance metrics on a regular basis, we’re demonstrating our unwavering commitment to the safe and scalable deployment of factory-built autonomous trucks. We believe it’s essential for partners, customers, regulators, and all road users to have visibility into our safety-driven progress and our disciplined approach toward commercializing autonomous driving technology.”

PlusAI has deployed autonomous driving technology across over five million miles of driving in the U.S., Europe, and Asia. These real-world operations have generated a proprietary dataset that fuels PlusAI’s technology development. Leveraging this data and advanced generative AI models, PlusAI has built a generalizable “driving intelligence” platform using auto-labeling, model distillation, and highly optimized in-vehicle neural networks.

## Safety Case Readiness

For safety assurance, PlusAI uses the safety case approach that is best practice in safety-critical industries including aviation, nuclear, automotive, and oil and gas. The PlusAI [Safety Case Readiness (SCR)](https://scf.plus.ai/) metric measures how mature and complete its underlying Safety Case Framework (SCF) is for SuperDrive to operate safely. The SCF is built on a multi-tiered structure of safety claims, sub-claims, and supporting evidence, organized around five core pillars that cover underlying architecture, processes, performance, and maintenance needed for safe operations. Specifically:

1. ***Understand*** – Establishes safety foundations through structured analysis, system definition, and hazard identification.
2. ***Design*** – Integrates safety principles, redundancy, and fault tolerance into the AV system’s architecture and software.
3. ***Develop*** – Verifies and validates system performance using simulation, bench tests, closed-course, and public road testing.
4. ***Prove*** – Measures safety performance through data analysis and continuous improvement of metrics and safety cases.
5. ***Deploy*** – Ensures safe deployment and maintenance through configuration control, release management, and in-field monitoring.

The PlusAI Safety Case Framework supports transparency and accountability by sharing key elements of the framework with stakeholders and by aligning with industry standards and best practices in automated vehicle safety assurance. It provides the basis for PlusAI’s risk-based approach to safety validation and helps inform regulatory engagement, operational readiness, and product maturity.

## Autonomous Miles Percentage

To assess the performance of its autonomous system, PlusAI uses the Autonomous Miles Percentage (AMP) metric. This is defined as the percentage of total distance driven by SuperDrive on a specified route that is completed under full autonomous control, without intervention from a remote operator or onboard safety driver. AMP reflects SuperDrive’s ability to sustain autonomous operation across varying conditions along a commercial corridor. AMP is a route-specific measure that quantifies the extent and reliability of SuperDrive in real-world operations. It complements PlusAI’s Remote Assistance Free Trips metric by providing a continuous measure of autonomous engagement across distance traveled and supports readiness assessments, regulatory engagement, and system maturity evaluation.

## Remote Assistance Free Trips

PlusAI’s Remote Assistance Free Trips (RAFT) measure captures the percentage of autonomous trips completed without any intervention from a remote operator or an onboard safety driver on a specified commercial route. A trip is considered RAFT-compliant if SuperDrive maintains full control from departure to arrival—without any human assistance to control the vehicle. While remote assistance will always be available if needed, this metric highlights SuperDrive’s operational independence, technical maturity, and readiness for scaled deployment.

“Our AV 2.0 architecture marks a major shift in how we design and deliver autonomous driving systems. By replacing hand-written components with end-to-end AI models, we've simplified the overall system and accelerated performance improvements. This approach ensures we'll be ready for broad deployment as soon as our factory-built autonomous trucks begin production in 2027. We're excited to be at the forefront of autonomous driving technology,” said Tim Daly, Chief Architect at PlusAI.

**AI performance soars in 2025 with compute scaling 4.4x yearly, LLM parameters doubling annually, and real-world capabilities outpacing traditional benchmarks.**

The artificial intelligence sector in 2025 has witnessed unprecedented acceleration, drastically altering the ways we measure and understand AI capabilities. While traditional benchmarks struggle to capture real-world utility, breakthrough performance metrics demonstrate that AI systems are evolving far faster than anticipated—with transformative implications for the remainder of this pivotal year.

[![Image 6: Artificial intelligence, AI - artistic impression. Image credit: Freepik, free license](https://www.sentisight.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/digital-art-ai-technology-background-768x432.jpg)](https://www.sentisight.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/digital-art-ai-technology-background-scaled.jpg)

The Exponential Scaling Revolution Behind Modern AI
---------------------------------------------------

The foundation of 2025’s AI breakthroughs lies in three interconnected scaling dimensions that [have reached critical mass](https://ourworldindata.org/scaling-up-ai).Since 2010, the computational resources used to train AI models have doubled approximately every six months, creating a 4.4x yearly growth rate that dwarfs previous technological advances. This represents a dramatic acceleration from the 1950-2010 period, when compute doubled roughly every two years.

[![Image 7: AI Benchmarks That Matter: Performance Soars in 2025 - SentiSight.ai](https://www.sentisight.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ai-in-business.jpeg)](https://www.sentisight.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ai-in-business.jpeg)
Image credit: HAI Stanford

Training data has experienced equally explosive growth, with datasets tripling in size annually since 2010. GPT-4’s training corpus of 13 trillion tokens—equivalent to over 2,000 times the entire English Wikipedia—exemplifies this data abundance. Meanwhile, model parameters have doubled yearly, culminating in systems like the QMoE model with 1.6 trillion parameters.

This scaling trifecta has produced capabilities that were theoretical just years ago. State-of-the-art systems that once struggled with basic counting now solve complex mathematical problems, generate realistic multimedia content, and engage in sophisticated academic discussions. The transition isn’t gradual—it manifests as sudden capability leaps when models reach specific size thresholds.

Real-World AI Capabilities vs. Academic Benchmarks
--------------------------------------------------

Perhaps the most striking revelation of 2025 is the profound disconnect between how AI is actually used and [how it’s typically evaluated](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.08253v1).Analysis of over four million real-world AI prompts reveals six core capabilities that dominate practical usage: Technical Assistance (65.1%), Reviewing Work (58.9%), Generation (25.5%), Information Retrieval (16.6%), Summarization (16.6%), and Data Structuring (4.0%).

Among 88% of AI users who are non-technical employees, the focus centers on collaborative tasks like writing assistance, document review, and workflow optimization—not the abstract problem-solving scenarios that dominate academic benchmarks. Current evaluation frameworks like MMLU and AIME, while measuring cognitive performance, fail to capture the conversational, iterative nature of human-AI collaboration.

For Technical Assistance, WebDev Arena emerges as the most realistic benchmark, using open-ended prompts that mirror actual help requests rather than narrowly defined Python functions. In Information Retrieval, SimpleQA provides more coherent fact-based interactions compared to rigid multiple-choice formats. However, critical capabilities like Reviewing Work and Data Structuring lack dedicated benchmarks entirely, despite their prevalence in real-world applications.

[![Image 8: AI Benchmarks That Matter: Performance Soars in 2025 - SentiSight.ai](blob:http://localhost/95f1eea50a2646f4f94b9987458c8d26)](https://www.sentisight.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ai-vs-human.jpeg)
Image credit: HAI Stanford

Performance Leadership in 2025’s Benchmark Landscape
----------------------------------------------------

When evaluated against capability-aligned metrics, [Google’s Gemini 2.5](https://www.sentisight.ai/gemini-2-5-pro-performance-analysis/) demonstrates remarkable versatility, ranking first in Summarization (89.1%), Generation (Elo score of 1458), and Technical Assistance (Elo score of 1420). Anthropic’s Claude secures second place in both Summarization (79.4%) and Technical Assistance (Elo score of 1357), highlighting the competitive intensity among leading models.

The research community has produced [significant advances throughout 2025](https://www.turing.com/resources/top-llm-trends), with papers like “Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test” showing GPT-4.5 achieving 73% human identification rates. Meanwhile, specialized systems like SWE-Lancer reveal current limitations—even top models succeed only 26.2% of the time on real freelance coding tasks, emphasizing the gap between benchmarks and applied performance.

The Rise of Agentic AI and Autonomous Systems
---------------------------------------------

The year 2025 already marks a fundamental shift [toward agentic AI](https://www.ibm.com/think/insights/ai-agents-2025-expectations-vs-reality)—systems capable of autonomous planning, reasoning, and action execution. Unlike traditional AI assistants requiring constant prompts, these agents break down complex tasks into manageable steps and execute them independently. IBM’s survey of 1,000 developers found 99% are exploring or developing AI agents, signaling industry-wide momentum.

However, experts remain divided on readiness. While underlying models possess sufficient capabilities—better reasoning, expanded context windows, and improved function calling—most organizations lack agent-ready infrastructure. The challenge isn’t model performance but enterprise API exposure and governance frameworks necessary for safe autonomous operation.

Autonomous agents represent a change of concept toward “experiential learning,” where AI systems learn through environmental interaction rather than static human data. This approach enables continuous adaptation and skill development, potentially driving the emergence of more general AI capabilities.

Efficiency Gains Outpace Traditional Scaling Advantages
-------------------------------------------------------

The competitive dynamics of 2025 reveal that [speed matters more than scale](https://www.pwc.com/us/en/tech-effect/ai-analytics/competing-in-age-of-ai.html), fundamentally altering traditional business advantages. AI-native organizations are achieving performance levels previously reserved for large incumbents through agentic approaches and efficient model deployment.

Smaller, more efficient models like TinyLlama (1.1B parameters) and Mixtral 8x7B demonstrate that performance doesn’t require massive size. These compact systems can operate with just 8GB of memory, making advanced AI accessible to mobile applications and resource-constrained environments.

Companies implementing AI solutions are regularly achieving 30% productivity improvements, with some organizations reporting human-AI collaboration productivity boosts of 50%. This represents a fundamental shift in workforce capability multiplication, where each employee can access specialized AI agent teams across multiple disciplines.

Multimodal Capabilities and Real-Time Integration
-------------------------------------------------

The evolution beyond text-only systems has accelerated dramatically in 2025. Models like GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet now process text, images, audio, and video in real-time, enabling new applications in creative tools, accessibility, and customer service.

Real-time fact-checking and external data access are becoming standard capabilities. Microsoft Copilot’s internet integration and models’ ability to provide citations by default address hallucination concerns while improving transparency and accuracy.

The emergence of synthetic training data represents another breakthrough, with Google’s self-improving models generating their own questions and answers to enhance performance. This technique reduces data collection costs while improving specialized domain performance.

Security, Governance, and Responsible AI Development
----------------------------------------------------

As AI systems gain autonomy, governance and security considerations have intensified. The scale of potential risks increases dramatically—while humans are limited by time and cognitive capacity, AI agents can execute actions rapidly and at scale, potentially causing cascading failures without proper oversight.

PwC’s 2024 Responsible AI Survey [found](https://www.pwc.com/us/en/tech-effect/ai-analytics/responsible-ai-survey.html) that only 11% of executives have fully implemented fundamental responsible AI capabilities. Effective governance must span risk management, audit controls, security, data governance, privacy, bias mitigation, and model performance monitoring.

Security risks identified by OWASP’s updated Top 10 for LLMs include system prompt leakage, excessive memory usage, and malicious prompt injection. Developers are implementing safeguards like sandboxed environments, output filters, and red teaming exercises to address these vulnerabilities.

[![Image 10: AI Benchmarks That Matter: Performance Soars in 2025 - SentiSight.ai](blob:http://localhost/51db8e272626c3d06e0faa0ab6f83709)](https://www.sentisight.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/medical-dev-ai.jpeg)
Image credit: HAI Stanford

Economic Impact and Market Transformation
-----------------------------------------

The economic implications of 2025’s AI advances are staggering. Goldman Sachs estimates generative AI could lift global GDP by 7% over the next decade, while the LLM market is projected to grow from $6.4 billion in 2024 to $36.1 billion by 2030.

Historical precedent suggests transformative potential. During the internet-fueled productivity boom ending in 2005, US labor productivity doubled to 2.8% annually. Current AI developments show similar—if not greater—potential to drive the next technology-powered economic expansion.

In PwC’s 28th Annual Global CEO Survey, 56% of CEOs report GenAI efficiency improvements in employee time usage, while 32% cite increased revenue and 34% report improved profitability. These early returns suggest much greater rewards as AI integration deepens.

[![Image 12: AI Benchmarks That Matter: Performance Soars in 2025 - SentiSight.ai](blob:http://localhost/be014031b9cf32b0f71d1de7715f9649)](https://www.sentisight.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ai-china-vs-us.jpeg)
Image credit: HAI Stanford

The Path Forward: Speed, Innovation, and Human-AI Collaboration
---------------------------------------------------------------

The scaling trends that powered 2025’s breakthroughs show no signs of slowing. Hardware improvements continue driving down costs while increasing performance, with GPU computing speed doubling every 2.5 years per dollar spent. Organizations are leveraging computational resources not just in training but also during inference, as demonstrated by OpenAI’s o1 model.

Domain-specific models are emerging as a key trend, with specialized systems like BloombergGPT for finance and Med-PaLM for healthcare delivering superior accuracy through deep contextual understanding. This represents a shift from one-size-fits-all toward targeted, industry-specific solutions.

The future workplace will be defined by human-AI collaboration rather than replacement. While AI handles routine tasks, humans remain essential for strategic direction, creative problem-solving, and ethical oversight. The most successful implementations will be those that augment human capabilities rather than attempt to supplant them entirely.

As 2025 progresses, the AI landscape continues evolving at unprecedented speed. The benchmarks that matter most are those reflecting real-world utility—measuring not just what AI can do, but how effectively it enhances human productivity and creativity. With more than half the year remaining, the trajectory suggests even more dramatic breakthroughs ahead, fundamentally reshaping how we work, create, and solve complex challenges.

title: Multi-KPI Testing: The Answer to Measurement in 2025

# Multi-KPI Testing: The Answer to Measurement in 2025

Nick Stoltz, Chief Strategy Officer

Published 10/15/2024

In today’s marketing world, measuring performance has never been more complex - or more crucial. Rising customer acquisition costs, AI-driven campaigns, and shifting consumer behaviors make it difficult for marketers to know exactly where to spend their next dollar. The key? Multi-KPI testing.

Let’s dive into why multi-KPI testing is essential for marketers in 2025 and how it can help brands get a clearer, more accurate picture of their marketing efforts.

## Why Incrementality Alone Isn’t Enough Anymore

According to [LoyaltyLion](https://loyaltylion.com/blog/how-to-use-loyalty-to-offset-rising-customer-acquisition-costs#:~:text=Unfortunately%2C%20acquisition%20costs%20are%20increasing,to%20change%20any%20time%20soon.), customer acquisition costs (CAC) are increasing every year, particularly in the world of eCommerce. We cover the reasons for rising costs in detail [in part one](https://www.measured.com/blog/part-1-is-your-attribution-sabotaging-your-customer-acquisition-efforts/), but let’s just highlight the fact that **acquisition costs have surged by 60% since 2019** **due to rising ad platform costs coupled with growing skepticism amongst marketers about where and how their ad spend is performing**. 

Incrementality testing, measuring the purchases or conversions that wouldn’t have happened without a specific marketing effort, has been a go-to method for measuring channel effectiveness for smart marketing organizations. However, heading into 2025, this approach alone is no longer adequate to fully understand your marketing performance and its implications for budgeting.

You might know how many incremental sales each channel drives, but do you understand the mix of new vs. existing customer purchases?  Do you understand what type of lift that marketing channel drives in KPIs further up the consideration cycle, like leads, visits, or awareness?  Do you know which of your channels more effectively drives higher LTV product sales?  Multi-KPI testing allows marketers to evaluate performance across multiple dimensions - e.g., new versus returning customers, the efficiency of each channel in driving product category sales, or boosting awareness or consideration.

## What is Multi-KPI Testing?

**Multi-KPI testing involves measuring more than just incremental orders. It’s about evaluating the total performance of a marketing channel across multiple key performance indicators (KPIs).** These KPIs should include total orders, new customer acquisition, high-value product purchases, leads, traffic, organic search volume, and even brand awareness metrics.

Are you accounting for the long-term impact of marketing and the awareness building that you need to fuel your brand’s growth? Your testing needs to account for how marketing vehicles drive incremental lift in awareness and consideration further up in the funnel, not just near-term sales.  Consideration lift carries value that purchase-only incrementality experiments won’t capture.

Let’s look at an example. Say you’re running Facebook ads. Instead of just tracking how many incremental orders are coming through, you should also ask:

* What percentage of those orders are from new customers?
* How does that compare to what Google Ads is driving?
* Are those new customers buying high-LTV products, or are they purchasing one-off, lower-value items?
* Are those ads driving lift in brand awareness and consideration?

The ability to test and, more importantly, optimize your media spend across multiple KPIs gives marketers a more comprehensive view of what’s working and what’s not, allowing them to make smarter decisions about where to allocate their budget that drive healthy and profitable long-term growth.

## The Importance of Testing for High-Lifetime Value Customers

One critical KPI that should be part of your Multi-KPI testing is customer lifetime value (LTV). Post-pandemic, many brands saw a surge in new customers thanks to deep discounts on promotional products. But here’s the catch: many of those customers didn’t stick around. They were drawn in by a deal, but they didn’t become repeat buyers.

When running Multi-KPI tests, focus on whether your channels are driving incremental lift in customers who buy high-LTV products and baskets. These are the customers who are likely to make repeat purchases and drive long-term revenue for your brand, not just one-and-done buyers.

Ask yourself:

* Am I attracting customers who will continue to purchase from my brand over time?
* Are my marketing channels driving high-value, repeat customers, or are they just bringing in low-value deal-hunters?

## Navigating the Confusion of AI Campaigns

AI-driven campaigns, such as Facebook’s Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns (ASC) and Google’s PMAX, [add a layer of complexity](https://www.measured.com/blog/part-1-is-your-attribution-sabotaging-your-customer-acquisition-efforts/) to marketing measurement. These campaigns can handle multiple functions - like prospecting, retargeting, and retention - all within a single ad campaign across multiple ad products. This makes it hard to tell exactly what each campaign is doing.

Before AI, you could run separate campaigns for prospecting new customers, retargeting existing visitors, and nurturing awareness. Today, AI campaigns bundle all these functions together, causing overlap with your existing traditional campaigns and making it harder to get a clear read on actual performance.  Measured recommends a best practice of beginning measurement journeys for AI campaigns by establishing multi-tactic baseline performance before using those insights to delve deeper into campaign performance.

To effectively measure the impact of AI campaigns, you need to test carefully, monitor closely, and ultimately consider a measurement roadmap to verify performance continually and evolve strategy. **Based on Measured’s experience, many brands often discover that their AI campaigns aren’t doing what they think they are, which can confuse reads and skew insights.**

Key takeaways for AI campaigns:

1) Create measurement journeys starting with multi-tactic tests to establish a baseline.

2) Set up tests carefully and closely monitor AI and standard campaign behavior during testing to ensure you're getting a clean signal.

3) Measure AI campaign performance via testing with multiple tests over the course of the year and use observations to evolve and hone strategy and campaign settings.

4) Expect that these AI campaigns, whether or not they’re effective, are very likely *not doing what you think they're doing.*

## Building a Holistic Framework for Multi-KPI Testing

Running Multi-KPI tests is just the start. Once you’ve gathered insights from your testing, you need to build a framework that connects these findings to decision-making and financial outcomes.

Here’s how you can structure this framework:

* **Measurement Framework:** Use your Multi-KPI testing to feed into your media mix model, which helps determine the long-term impact of upper-funnel channels like awareness campaigns. This should, in turn, inform your attribution models, giving you a clear view of how each channel performs across multiple KPIs.
* **Financial Framework**: Use the insights from your testing to guide monthly budgeting and campaign optimizations. Use testing and modeling to build a bridge with your finance team that aligns marketing toward clear goals.  Are you trying to hit a specific revenue target? Perhaps every marketing dollar needs to hit a defined contribution margin.  Or perhaps you’re aiming for a specific customer acquisition cost defined by customer lifetime value and time to pay back guided by your brand’s financial strategy?
* **Decision Framework:** Define your budget to achieve these goals and align your budget allocation to maximize outcomes. Ultimately, your tests should help you answer questions like:

* + How do I set the right budget based on these performance insights?
  + What am I willing to pay for a new customer based on their projected LTV?
  + How am I pacing towards goals, and how can I make adjustments as needed?

By implementing this framework, you’ll be able to leverage your Multi-KPI testing to not only understand your channel performance but also make informed financial decisions that drive growth.

## Conclusion

The marketing landscape today is complex, but **multi-KPI testing provides a powerful solution for cutting through the confusion and getting a clearer picture of your marketing performance.** By testing across multiple KPIs and building a robust decision-making framework, you’ll be better equipped to optimize your budget and drive long-term growth.

### What Exactly *Is* an AI KPI?

It’s **not** just accuracy. It’s the **quantifiable heartbeat** of your AI system across **technical**, **operational**, and **ethical** dimensions. Think of KPIs as the **OKRs** your model would set for itself—if it could talk.

## 🧩 Types of AI KPIs: From Model Metrics to Business Value

*Video: How To develop great KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) for your business, department or project.*

### 1. Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score

**Accuracy** alone is like bragging about your golf score while ignoring the wind. Combine it with **precision/recall** and you get the **F1**—the harmonic mean that keeps ML engineers humble.

| Metric | When to Use | Pro Tip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accuracy | Balanced datasets | Watch out for **class imbalance** |
| Precision | When **false positives** hurt (spam filters) | Tune threshold aggressively |
| Recall | When **false negatives** hurt (cancer screening) | Use **weighted loss** |
| F1 | Always | Report **macro & micro** variants |

🔗 **Deep dive:** [What are the key benchmarks for evaluating AI model performance?](https://www.chatbench.org/what-are-the-key-benchmarks-for-evaluating-ai-model-performance/)

---

### 2. Model Robustness and Reliability

We once deployed a **credit-risk model** that worked beautifully—until the **COVID-19 data drift** hit. Cue frantic Slack messages at 3 a.m.  
Key KPIs:

* **Adversarial accuracy** (think **FGSM attacks**)
* **Noise tolerance** (add Gaussian blur, retest)
* **Chaos engineering score** (how gracefully it fails)

---

### 3. AI Fairness and Bias Metrics

Use **IBM AI Fairness 360** or **Google’s What-If Tool** to track:

* **Demographic parity difference**
* **Equal opportunity difference**
* **Calibration error across groups**

> “Fairness isn’t a feature—it’s a **baseline requirement**.” — Timnit Gebru

---

### 4. Explainability and Interpretability KPIs

**LIME** and **SHAP** are cool, but stakeholders want **one number**. We created the **Explainability Index**:

```
EI = (1 – avg. |SHAP| entropy) × 100

```

Higher EI = easier to explain to your legal team.

---

### 5. Operational Efficiency: Latency, Throughput, and Uptime

| KPI | SLO Example | Tooling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **P99 latency** | < 250 ms | Prometheus + Grafana |
| **Throughput** | 10 k req/sec | **K6** load tests |
| **Uptime** | 99.9 % | **Datadog** synthetic checks |

---

### 6. User Engagement and Adoption Rates

Track **DAU/MAU**, **feature adoption funnel**, and **time-to-first-value**.  
**Hotjar** heatmaps revealed our chatbot’s “reset” button was clicked 42 % of the time—**ouch**.

---

### 7. Business Impact: ROI, Cost Savings, and Revenue Growth

We helped a fintech client **cut fraud losses by 28 %**—but only after we tied the model’s **precision@k** directly to **$ saved**.  
Formula:

```
ROI = (Net $ Benefit – AI Cost) / AI Cost × 100

```

---

### 8. Ethical and Regulatory Compliance KPIs

Create a **compliance scorecard**:

| Regulation | KPI | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GDPR | Right-to-explanation requests resolved | < 30 days |
| EU AI Act | High-risk system audit pass rate | 100 % |
| SOC 2 | Control failures | 0 |

---

### 9. Continuous Learning and Model Drift Detection

Use **Evidently AI** to monitor:

* **PSI > 0.2** triggers retraining
* **Data quality score** (missing values, schema drift)

---

### 10. Customer Satisfaction and NPS for AI Solutions

We run **in-product micro-surveys** (“Was this AI helpful?”) and pipe the **CSAT** straight into **Amplitude**.

---

### 11. Security and Privacy Metrics for AI Systems

* **Differential privacy ε < 1**
* **Membership inference attack success rate < 5 %**
* **Model encryption at rest** ✅

## ❓ FAQ

### What are the most important Key Performance Indicators for measuring the success of AI initiatives in a business setting?

The most important KPIs vary by context but generally include:

* **Model Quality Metrics:** Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score to ensure technical soundness.
* **Operational Metrics:** Latency, throughput, uptime for system reliability.
* **Business Impact KPIs:** ROI, cost savings, revenue growth, and customer satisfaction (e.g., NPS).
* **Ethical and Compliance KPIs:** Fairness scores, bias detection, and regulatory adherence.

These KPIs collectively ensure AI initiatives deliver measurable value aligned with business objectives.

### How can organizations effectively track and evaluate the performance of their AI systems to drive continuous improvement?

Effective tracking requires:

* **Automated monitoring pipelines** using tools like Metaflow, Evidently AI, or Prometheus.
* **Real-time dashboards** with alerts for KPI deviations.
* **Regular KPI reviews** involving cross-functional teams to interpret data and prioritize improvements.
* **Adaptive thresholds** that evolve with data drift and changing business conditions.

Continuous feedback loops enable proactive model retraining and system tuning.

### What role do Key Performance Indicators play in ensuring AI solutions are aligned with overall business objectives and strategic goals?

KPIs translate abstract business goals into concrete, measurable targets for AI teams. They:

* **Bridge communication gaps** between technical and business stakeholders.
* **Prioritize AI development efforts** on features that maximize business value.
* **Enable accountability** by making AI performance transparent and actionable.
* **Support strategic agility** by highlighting when pivots or investments are needed.

Without KPIs, AI risks becoming a siloed technology rather than a strategic asset.

### How can companies use Key Performance Indicators to compare the performance of different AI models and algorithms, and make data-driven decisions about their AI investments?

Companies should:

* Establish **standardized KPI frameworks** across projects to ensure apples-to-apples comparisons.
* Use **benchmark datasets** and metrics like precision@k, latency, and fairness scores.
* Incorporate **business KPIs** such as cost savings or revenue impact alongside technical metrics.
* Leverage **ensemble KPIs** that combine multiple indicators for holistic evaluation.
* Perform **A/B testing** and shadow deployments to validate KPI improvements in production.

This approach enables confident, data-driven AI investment decisions.

### How do ethical and regulatory KPIs influence AI development and deployment?

Ethical and regulatory KPIs act as guardrails ensuring AI systems:

* Avoid discriminatory outcomes by monitoring bias and fairness.
* Maintain transparency through explainability metrics.
* Comply with laws like GDPR and the EU AI Act to avoid legal and reputational risks.
* Foster user trust, which is critical for adoption and long-term success.

Ignoring these KPIs can result in costly penalties and loss of stakeholder confidence.

AI KPIs are essential for **assessing different AI models**, as well as the effectiveness of business implementation.We’ve put together a comprehensive list of **34 AI and automation KPIs** you can use to assess both.

‍

## 34 AI KPIs to Use in Business

The success of your [AI initiatives](https://www.multimodal.dev/post/how-to-get-buy-in-from-stakeholders-for-ai-initiatives) doesn't just come down to model performance. It also depends on a variety of other factors the model’s robustness, accuracy, quality of data, integration abilities and more. The KPIs below will help you measure all of these aspects.

### Assessing AI Models - Evaluating Effectiveness and Efficiency

**1) Accuracy**

Accuracy pertains to how often and correctly an AI model **predicts outcomes**. It’s an essential KPI for evaluating model performance, ensuring reliable results, minimizing errors, and improving effectiveness.

This KPI can show how well an AI model understands data and how accurate its processing of data is.

**2) Precision and recall**

Precision KPI helps showcase the AI model’s ability to [make true positive predictions](https://research.aimultiple.com/machine-learning-accuracy/) while disregarding false positives. This helps ensure **higher relevancy** **and quality** of predicted outcomes.

Recall indicator can evaluate the model’s true positive predictions compared to all positive instances in the data. This helps reduce false negatives, improve correctness, and eliminate the possibility of a missing positive instance leading to big consequences for the business.

‍**3) F1 score**

F1 score is a performance metric that combines precision and recall KPI in one number to provide an easier AI evaluation. This KPI helps **balance precision measures** against recall measures to give the exact number of actual positives.

This metric is useful for dealing with uneven classes and datasets as it ensures the AI model performs better in identifying relevant cases and minimizes incorrect predictions.

‍**4) Area under the ROC curve (AUR-ROC)**

AUR-ROC measures the model’s capability to differentiate between positive and negative classes. A higher [AUR-ROC value](https://www.simplilearn.com/what-is-a-roc-curve-and-how-to-use-it-in-performance-modeling-article) indicates **better identification of positive cases** while minimizing false alarms.

This is a valuable metric to assess classification models and their accuracy.

### Assessing Data Quality - Evaluating Data for Higher Reliability and Performance

**5) Completeness**

Data completeness shows **if all needed data is available** in the dataset. High completeness ensures no information is missing, which is crucial for the AI’s accurate training and analysis.

Incomplete data leads to unreliable results which can impact business decisions, which is why we highly recommend determining completeness.

**6) Timelines**

Outdated data can lead to incorrect insights, which affects AI’s performance. Measuring the timeline indicator helps you understand how up-to-date your data is.

High timelines mean that data reflects the **most current information**, which leads to better accuracy and relevant decisions. This metric can be especially useful if you’re [training an AI model using your data](https://www.multimodal.dev/post/training-an-llm-with-custom-data).

**7) Uniqueness**

Uniqueness measures duplicates within the dataset. High uniqueness ensures that each data point is only recorded once, which helps **prevent redundancy** and ensures better data integrity.

Duplicate data can distort insights and lead to inaccurate outcomes.

**8) Integrity**

Integrity indicator measures the accuracy and reliability of data relationship with the dataset.

Higher integrity indicates **correct and maintained consistency**, which supports a better decision-making process. Poor data integrity, on the other hand, can lead to flawed AI outcomes, errors, and misinterpretations.

**9) Accessibility**

Data accessibility indicates how accessible data is to users and other systems. High accessibility leads to **better data availability** for model training and analysis without disruptions.

Limited accessibility can reduce the effectiveness of the AI’s model to promptly make accurate decisions.

**10) Error rate**

Error rate indicators can **measure dataset anomalies**. The lower error indicates high-quality and reliable data. Higher error rates can lead to incorrect predictions, flawed insights, and inaccuracies that can negatively impact business decisions.

**11) Bias detection**

A bias detection indicator is useful in **measuring the presence of biases** within the dataset. Effective bias detection leads to better data representation, which reduces the risk of distorted outcomes.

Undetected bias can lead to discriminatory decisions and undermine the fairness and reliability of the AI model.

**12) Data quality score**

A data quality score is a metric that **combines various indicators** of data quality, like accuracy, completeness, consistency, and timelines, into one score. A higher data quality score ensures that data meets high standards across all quality dimensions, which ensures better accuracy and reliability.

### Analyzing Performance - Gaining a Clear Understanding of Model’s Operational Efficiency

**13) Response time**

Response time helps measure the time it takes the AI model to deliver results after receiving an input. Shorter response times lead to faster and **more efficient systems**, which is important for real-time apps.

It’s highly recommended to measure this key performance indicator to [ensure a lower response time](https://www.multimodal.dev/customer-stories/sales-data-management-ai) and maintain a smooth user experience, which improves user satisfaction.

**14) Throughput**

Throughput is an indicator that measures the number of tasks an AI system can process in a specific time frame. Higher throughput indicates better performance and higher efficiency, which means that the AI model can **handle more requests simultaneously**.

It’s a good idea to track this KPI for AI models that have a direct impact on productivity and user satisfaction, as it can help you understand how responsive your AI model is.

**15) Error rate**

The error rate is a simple indicator that helps determine the **ratio of incorrect outputs** produced by the AI model compared to the total number of generated outputs. A lower error rate indicates a much better AI performance with higher accuracy and reliability.

We highly recommend monitoring the error rate indicator to maintain your AI model’s quality and performance levels.

**16) Robustness**

A robust AI model can **maintain** **consistent performance** across a variety of inputs, which includes unexpected data. The robustness indicator will show how adaptable an AI model is to various scenarios without a drop in accuracy and reliability.

This indicator can also give insight into how effective an AI model is in real-world use.

### Assessing AI’s Business Impact - Measuring Tangible Business Benefits

**17) Cost savings**

Cost savings measure the reduction in expenses achieved through AI’s automation efforts. For example, you can track the reduced costs associated with labor, resources, and time-to-decision.

Tracking cost savings can help businesses **track the** **financial impact** of their AI investment.

‍**18) Time savings**

Time savings indicate the reduction in time needed to complete tasks after the implementation of AI solutions. **Automation of repetitive tasks** and enhancement of decision-making processes help speed up task execution.

Monitoring this indicator can help the organization improve productivity and efficiency, and achieve a **better overall resource allocation**.

**19) Revenue growth**

Revenue growth indicators measure **growth in sales** and new business opportunities generated with AI’s help.

Leveraging [AI solutions](https://www.multimodal.dev/banking) can help tailor and personalize products and services to improve customer experience, and also lead to the company’s revenue growth by, for example, allowing you to serve more customers in less time.

Tracking the growth helps assess the **financial benefits** of [AI implementation](https://www.multimodal.dev/post/how-to-implement-ai-in-business) and also refine automation strategy when needed.

**20) Customer satisfaction**

AI can improve customer experience in many ways and this indicator helps track those improvements after the AI implementation. Monitoring this key indicator can help businesses **understand user needs**, enhance and customize their product offerings, and eventually improve retention and growth.

**21) Employee productivity**

Employee productivity **measures the increase in output per employee** after the AI implementation and automation of repetitive and labor-intensive tasks.

With such automation initiatives, employees get a chance to focus on higher-value work, while companies that track employee productivity can evaluate the impact of AI on the workforce’s productivity and efficiency.

### Analyzing User Experience - Improving Interaction Quality

**22) Customer effort score**

CES measures how easy it is for users to achieve their goals using the AI system. A lower score indicates a user-friendly experience but also **reduced effort** required for completing tasks. This indicator helps businesses track friction points, but also learn how they can enhance overall user experience.

**23) Task success rate**

Task success rate is a similar indicator to customer effort score, but it measures the percentage of successfully completed tasks **by any end user** — including employees. A higher success percentage indicates AI’s effectiveness, which shows how well the AI solution meets the user’s needs.

**24) Time on task**

Time on task indicators measure the **time users take to complete tasks** using the AI solution. A shorter time indicates an efficient and user-friendly experience.

By measuring this metric, businesses can evaluate the AI’s useability, streamline processes, and reduce user effort in task completion.

**25) User retention rate**

The user retention rate indicates the percentage of users who continue using the AI system. Higher retention rates indicate a satisfying user experience and great engagement. This metric helps **assess the long-term value** of the company’s AI model but also ensures the model meets user needs.

You can also use this metric to evaluate customer satisfaction, as described above.

**26) Latency**

The latency metric measures the AI’s response time from the user’s perspective, where **lower latency indicates faster interactions** and better user experience. It’s highly recommended to measure latency for real-time AI systems.This indicator can help you improve overall [system efficiency](https://osiglobal.com/the-impact-of-ai-on-data-center-bandwidth-and-latency/), ensuring enhanced user experience and less frustration.

**27) Helpdesk inquiries**

The helpdesk inquiries indicator measures the **number of received support requests** or questions regarding the AI system. Fewer inquiries indicate a user-friendly experience.

A higher number of helpdesk inquiries can help businesses identify pain points that need work, which eventually leads to better satisfaction and efficiency.

### Assessing Compliance and Ethics - Ensuring Legal Compliance

**28) Regulatory compliance rate**

The regulatory compliance measures a percentage of AI processes and outputs that **adhere to relevant regulations**, industry standards, and laws. A high compliance rate indicates good AI system operation within legal frameworks, with correct risk mitigation and ethical practices in place.

Relying on this indicator helps maintain trust and accountability for the AI solution.

**29) Ethical standards adherence**

Ethical standards adherence evaluates to which extent the AI model complies with ethical guidelines. A higher adherence rate can indicate **AI’s fairness**, transparency, accountability, minimized bias, and responsible use.

**30) Data privacy and security scores**

This indicator measures the effectiveness of practices that **protect sensitive user information** and compliance with data protection regulations. Higher data privacy and security scores ensure better security against unauthorized access and breaches.

Monitoring this KPI helps maintain user trust, protects the company’s reputation, and adheres to legal obligations.

**31) Audit frequency and results**

This KPI measures how often an AI system is audited, as well as the outcomes of those audits. Higher audit frequency means positive results that indicate **regular and thorough examination** of AI processes.

This ensures the AI model meets compliance, ethical standards, and expected performance. Therefore, measuring this metric can help you maintain transparency while continuously improving the AI model.

### Analyzing Return on Investment - Measuring Financial Success, Returns, and Business Growth

**32) ROI**

ROI measures the return on AI investment relative to its cost. This indicator helps businesses **assess progress and the effectiveness of AI projects** in generating revenue and cutting costs.

If you need help calculating an AI ROI, check out our [AI ROI calculation](https://www.multimodal.dev/post/how-to-calculate-ai-roi) post or [ask our experts](https://www.multimodal.dev/contact-us) to calculate AI ROI for your business.

**33) Market share growth**

Market share growth represents the growtha company experiences after implementing AI. This indicator reflects **competitive positioning**, customer acquisition, and retention. A higher number always indicates successful AI strategies in the expansion of a company’s presence.

**34) Scalability and flexibility**

Scalability measures the **AI’s ability to expand** its capabilities without compromising its performance. The flexibility indicator assesses the AI’s ability to adapt to new tasks or changes, where a higher score ensures that AI can grow with the business.

## FAQs

### How do you measure the performance of Gen AI?

Measuring Gen AI’s performance ensures **better effectiveness** and optimization of its use in various case scenarios. Key performance indicators are crucial as they help **evaluate the outputs** across various integrations.This is what **measuring the performance of Gen AI** looks like:

1. Defining business objectives and use cases
2. Selecting appropriate KPIs to measure performance
3. Collecting the model’s input and output data
4. Evaluating collected data according to chosen KPIs
5. Comparing results with projections
6. Analyzing results and continuously monitoring and improving

Identifying goals and **setting use cases** early on in the measurement process is important. This will help you choose relevant KPIs you can take measures against.

After you have measured the performance for a variety of KPIs, you can **compare the results** with projections made before the AI implementation.

Such a comparison will help you **measure AI’s performance metrics** like accuracy, efficiency, performance, its impact on your business, and additional metrics.

### Can I use these KPIs for test automation?

Yes, you can use KPIs for test automation to gain insights into the effectiveness of the test automation efforts, which can also help you identify areas for improvement.

Some of the best KPIs for test automation include:

* Execution time
* Automation rate
* Time to feedback
* Return on investment
* Cost savings
* Test maintenance effort

### Should I opt for manual or automated testing?

Choosing between manual and automated testing depends on the size of the project, complexity, budget, and goals. Here’s a quick guide to help you make the right choice for your needs.

Test automation KPIs are ideal if you’re dealing with:

* Many repetitive tasks
* Large test cases
* Continuous integration
* Performance testing
* Testing across multiple platforms

Automation testing is also ideal if you want to achieve better long-term cost efficiency after the testing process. If you’re dealing with complex projects, automation testing teams can help simplify the process.

However, if you’re dealing with the following cases, you might want to opt in for manual testing:

* Exploratory testing
* Short-term projects
* Frequent changes
* Complex user interaction
* User experience testing

Keep in mind that you can combine both manual and automated tests for a balanced approach that leads to high-quality results.

### What are the benefits of using AI KPIs?

Using AI KPIs helps:

* Improve the automation testing process
* Improve testing skills and testing efforts
* Measure performance
* Make data-driven decisions with higher accuracy
* Drive continuous improvement
* Ensure transparency and accountability
* Allocate resources better
* Manage risk early in the AI development process
* Improve user satisfaction

There are many more benefits, depending on the way you implement AI in your business and which KPIs you choose.
